speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after a tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly when this pain started and what specific activities trigger it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of recurrent ear infections, recent tympanoplasty, and the specific nature of your pain triggered by chewing and pressure from earrings, I am concerned about a graft issue or new infection. Could you describe if you have noticed any fluid drainage, fullness, or a popping sensation in your right ear recently? REQUEST TEST: Pure_Tone_Audiometry (to correlate with the previous report); REQUEST IMAGES: Otoscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pure_Tone_Audiometry: Findings consistent with one-week-old report, showing improved hearing by 20 decibels post tympanoplasty; Otoscopy: Right ear canal shows intact graft with no evidence of fluid drainage, fullness, or active infection; Left ear canal clear; Tympanic membranes bilaterally appear intact.

speaker: Doctor
text: The audiometry and otoscopy results are reassuring, showing an intact graft and no active infection. Since your pain is specifically triggered by eating (chewing) and wearing earrings (pressure), could you confirm if you also feel a distinct "popping" or clicking sensation in your ear during these movements?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Superior Semicanalicular Neuralgia (specifically involving the Greater Auricular or Arnold's nerve) due to post-tympanoplasty graft tension or suture impingement on the superficial temporal nerve, exacerbated by mechanical stimulation from chewing and earrings.
